The present claim petition is filed against the respondent under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest for the death of Subhash Sheshrao Mhasaye in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.07.2024.
SCCH-10 2.

The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 15.07.2024 at about 7.45 p.m., one Subhash Sheshrao Mhasaye @ Nikhil was walking on extreme side of Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, in front of Dayanandasagar college, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-06- F-0897 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to said Subhash Sheshrao Mhasaye from behind.
Due to the impact, he sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 43 years and he was a driver cum Mason and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.
Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-06-F-0897.
As such, the respondent being owner is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petition.

sentences.text: In response to the Petition notice, the respondent has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The contentions of the respondent in brief are as under:
The respondent contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable.
The respondent has denied the accident, manner of accident and rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 06-F-0897.
The respondent has also denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased and also age, avocation and income of the deceased.
It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased who without noticing the moving bus, came before it and met with an accident.
As per the FIR, the deceased was a beggar and also mentally not conscious and he stayed in that locality as Nikhil since two years.
The petition is filed for wrongful gain.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent prayed for SCCH-10 dismissal of the petition against it.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 15.07.2024 at about 7.45 p.m., when the deceased Subhash Sheshrao Mhasay @ Nikhil was walking on extreme left side of Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, in front of Dayanandasagar College, Udipalya,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South, at that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-F-0897 driven from Bengaluru towards Kanakapura in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and he sustained severe injuries all over the body and succumbed to the said injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased Subash Sheshrao Mhasaye @ Nikhil ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4) What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
On the other hand, the respondent examined its SCCH-10 Driver as RW-1, but not produced any documents.
7. Heard arguments.

Perused the materials available on record.

My finding to the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 :

As per final order,

 R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioners have filed the present petition seeking compensation on account of death of Subhash Sheshrao Mhasaye @ Nikhil in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15-07-2024.
10.

According to the petitioners, deceased was pedestrian on extreme left side of Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, in front of Dayanandasagar college, Udipalya, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-06-F-0897 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to said Subhash SCCH-10 Sheshrao Mhasaye from behind.
Due to the impact, he sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
11. To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR in crime No.0242/2024 of Kaggalipura PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 it reveal that, I.O.
has registered a case against the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-F-0897 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 106 and 281 of BNS.
Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet filed by the Kaggalipura police against one Mr. Vishnusgar. K, who is none other than the driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 are Inquest and the Postmortem report respectively.
On perusal of postmortem report, it reveals that the deceased died due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of injuries sustained in the accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of SCCH-10 the offending vehicle and deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the accident.
12. The respondent has seriously disputed the negligent driving of driver of the vehicle.
The respondent has examined the Conductor of the offending vehicle as RW-1.

Though RW-1 in his chief examination affidavit has stated that the accident occurred not due to negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle, during the cross-examination he has stated that, at the time of accident he was issuing tickets to the passengers and he has not witnessed how the accident occurred.
Hence, based on the evidence of RW-1, it cannot be said that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased.
Therefore, the evidence of RW1 is not helpful to the respondent to establish that the driver of the offending vehicle was not negligent.
13. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view receives support from SCCH-10 the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case Vaishali Subhaash Mhasaye vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130767218/
4 of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
14.

sentences.text: Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-F-0897 and the deceased Shubhash Sheshrao Mhasaye succumbed to the fatal injuries at the spot in the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-
It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 daughters, petitioner No.4 is the son, the petitioner No.5 and 6 are the parents of the deceased.
In order to prove the relationship SCCH-10 with the deceased, the petitioners have produced copies of Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 Statement of Marks card of petitioner No.2.
On perusal of Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 it reveal that, the petitioners are the wife, daughters, son and parents of deceased.
Further, the respondents have not so seriously disputed the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.3:
It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, deceased was hale and healthy at the time of accident, he was aged 43 years and he was a driver cum Mason and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased they put to great hardship and lost their bread earner of the family.
17. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have SCCH-10 not produced any documents.
On perusal of PM report as per Ex.P.7, wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 43 years.

Therefore,
this Tribunal considers the age of the deceased as 43 years at the time of accident.
18. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any document.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2022, the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the SCCH-10 letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 15.07.2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the deceased.

Before proceeding to award compensation under the different heads, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in para No.61 has proceeded to record the following conclusions;
(iv) In case the deceased was self- employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established SCCH-10 income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
20. As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 14 is applicable for the age group of 41 to 45 years.

21. In the instant case, the deceased left behind his wife (petitioner No.1), children (petitioner No.2 to 4), father SCCH-10 (petitioner No.5) and mother (petitioner No.6) and they are dependents of the deceased.

In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses, where the number of dependents are 4 to 6, the deduction would be 1/4th.
As discussed supra, in the present case, Petitioner No.1 to 6 of the deceased are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/4th of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.16,500/- and annual income would be Rs.1,98,000/-.

If 1/4 th is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,48,500/-.
22.

As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 25% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was under the age group of 40-50 years.

In the SCCH-10 present case, the deceased was aged 43 years at the time of accident Vaishali Subhaash Mhasaye vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130767218/
6 and was self employed.

sentences.text: Hence, an addition of 25% shall be added to Rs.1,48,500/-, it would be Rs.1,85,625/-.
The multiplier will be 14 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (43 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,85,625/- X 14 = Rs.25,98,750/-.
Thus, Rs.25,98,750/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

23. As per Pranay Sethi Case, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years from the date of judgment (31.10.2017).
Therefore, in the instant case, the petitioners are entitled for the aforesaid conventional heads with enhanced rate of 20%.

24. In Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Ors., (Civil Appeal SCCH-10 No.9581/2018), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the children are entitled for parental consortium and parents are entitled for filial consortium;

sentences.text: 7 As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-F-0897.

As far as liability is concerned, the respondent who is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending KSRTC bus, the respondent has to pay the compensation of Rs.29,22,750/- along with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
According to the respondent, soon after the accident they have paid a sum of Rs.25,000/- to the petitioners towards interim compensation.
Further, the petitioners have also admitted the receipt of said interim compensation amount.

Hence,
the said interim SCCH-10 compensation has to be deducted from total compensation amount awarded by this Tribunal.
After deducting Rs.25,000/-, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,97,750/- along with interest in the ratio of 20:20:20:20:10:10 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

28. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,97,750/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled to receive SCCH-10 compensation in the ratio of 20:20:20:20:10:10 respectively from the date of this order.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount of petitioner No.1 shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of her choice and balance amount shall be released to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.2 shall be invested in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.

The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.3 and 4, shall be invested in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank of petitioners'
choice till they attain the age of majority.
SCCH-10 The entire compensation awarded to petitioner No.5 and 6 shall be released to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

23. As per Pranay Sethi Case, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years from the date of judgment (31.10.2017).
Therefore, in the instant case, the petitioners are entitled for the aforesaid conventional heads with enhanced rate of 20%.
As discussed above, since Loss of estate, Loss of Consortium and Funeral expenses has been fixed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi Case, the petitioners are entitled to receive Rs.18,000/-, Rs.48,000/-each (Petitioner No.1 to 6) and Rs.18,000/- respectively for loss of Estate,
Spousal, Parental and filial consortium and funeral expenses.
26. From the above discussions the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl. Heads Compensation No.
1. Loss of dependency Rs.25,98,750/-
4. Loss of filial consortium to petitioner Rs. 96,000/-
SCCH-10 No.5 & 6 (father and mother)

As far as liability is concerned, the respondent who is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending KSRTC bus, the respondent has to pay the compensation of Rs.29,22,750/- along with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Hence,
the said interim SCCH-10 compensation has to be deducted from total compensation amount awarded by this Tribunal.
After deducting Rs.25,000/-, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,97,750/- along with interest in the ratio of 20:20:20:20:10:10 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,97,750/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled to receive SCCH-10 compensation in the ratio of 20:20:20:20:10:10 respectively from the date of this order.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount of petitioner No.1 shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of her choice and balance amount shall be released to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.2 shall be invested in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.3 and 4, shall be invested in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank of petitioners'
choice till they attain the age of majority.
SCCH-10 The entire compensation awarded to petitioner No.5 and 6 shall be released to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
